blocks.x: What the September 2026 Winnipeg housing market numbers say

The [Winnipeg Regional Real Estate Board's September 2026 release](https://www.winnipegregionalrealestatenews.com/market-statistics/market-releases/article/629/more-choice-record-average-prices-and-softer-sales-defined-september-results) shows a Winnipeg housing market shifting under sellers' feet. There were 1,250 sales in September, down about 10% from a year earlier, though even with the five-year average. At the same time, active listings climbed to 4,234, up about 14%, and detached-home listings rose roughly 20%.
Prices have not cracked: the year-to-date average for detached homes across the board's market region is $467,687, a record. But the balance of power is moving.

That combination, record prices with softer sales and more inventory, can be an early signal of a market where buyers start to negotiate harder. Sellers can still get strong prices, but buyers have more homes to compare.
These figures cover the board's whole market region, not only the city.
Our view: inventory turns curb appeal from nice-to-have into a pricing tool
In a tight market, buyers forgive a peeling fascia or a faded front door because there is little else to see. In a market with 14% more listings, they are less likely to. Some may scroll past it.
The first photo in a listing is usually the front of the house, and it is competing with other front-of-house photos in the same price band.

The interest-rate picture adds pressure. On October 28, 2026, the Bank of Canada [raised its policy rate to 2.50%](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2026/10/fad-press-release-2026-10-28/), its first increase since July 2023, and signalled that more increases are possible. Buyers who were stretching their budgets now have less room, and they may be pickier about homes that look like they need work.
A buyer who sees "needs paint" sees a cost they may subtract from their offer, possibly more than the job would actually cost.

That is why we think professional [exterior painting services](/services/exterior-painting) belong near the top of every pre-listing conversation. Paint is not a cover-up; it is one of the most visible signals that a home has been maintained.
Where exterior work shows first
Not every exterior project is worth doing before a sale. The items most likely to matter are the ones a buyer sees first:
**Front door and trim.** A repainted or [replaced front door](/services/windows-and-doors) changes how the house looks in the listing photo.
**Fascia, soffit and window trim.** Peeling paint around windows can read as water damage, even when it is not.
**Garage door and siding touch-ups.** Where the garage faces the street, it is a big part of the first photo.
**Masonry and steps.** Cracked parging or crumbling front steps can read as structural problems to buyers and inspectors alike.
**Fences and decks that face the street.** A grey, weathered fence is not neutral in photos.
The Winnipeg timing problem

Exterior paint needs warm, dry conditions to cure properly. In Winnipeg, [exterior painting is done between late spring and early fall](/blog/exterior-painting-winnipeg-when-to-paint), and the paint's label sets the exact limits. That leaves sellers with three practical paths:
**Listing now:** focus on cleaning, minor touch-ups where conditions allow, and interior presentation, and price to reflect any visible exterior wear.

**Listing in spring:** book exterior work now for the first suitable weeks, usually in late spring. Contractors' spring calendars can fill early, and sellers who wait until April can end up listing late.
**Holding and renting:** if a sale is not urgent, use the winter to plan masonry, door and window work, and book it for the warmer months.
For agents, the second path is the one worth raising with any client who is "thinking about spring." A conversation this winter is what gets the house photographed in May.
What agents should tell sellers now

The honest message is that prices are holding but buyers are getting choosier. That gives agents a credible, data-backed reason to recommend [pre-listing work](/blog/pre-listing-renovations-winnipeg) without sounding like they are padding the budget.

Bring the board's latest numbers to the listing appointment. Point out the extra inventory in the seller's price range. Then walk the outside of the house with the seller and list the five things a buyer will notice from the sidewalk.

A short exterior scope, priced in a written quote after a free on-site visit, gives the seller a clear choice: invest in presentation, or accept that buyers may negotiate off the asking price for the same issues.
